chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was asked: 'Which charity is the most superior?' He said: 'Upon the generous relative (of kinship).'
ai.seo_question: What is the most superior form of charity according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the most superior charity is directed toward a relative who is 'kashih'—a term often interpreted in Shia scholarship as one who is generous, eager, or actively maintaining kinship ties, rather than merely possessing wealth. This highlights the Shia emphasis on *silat al-rahim* (maintaining kinship) as a spiritual multiplier for charitable acts, distinguishing it from general almsgiving. The narration underscores the practical implication that supporting relatives who actively uphold family bonds yields greater spiritual reward than giving to strangers.
